clue.text: A drink cures heart-break!

indicators.note: a break smashes something into pieces, so the letters of the two words before it are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A tipple is offered as a cure for a broken heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' tells you to rearrange CURES HEART into a ten-letter green or yellow liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Form a company of thespians

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a theatre troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A mould or shape is a cast, and the full set of actors in a play is likewise called its cast.

clue.text: Think people should be allowed in at pleasure

indicators.note: being allowed in means entering, so these pieces go inside the word at

parts.note: taken as written
to muse is to think or ponder
men are people

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the public be admitted whenever they like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be allowed in' is the container signal; 'Think' looks like the start of an instruction but is a verb meaning ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is enjoyment or entertainment, a close synonym of delight.

clue.text: Some actresses have beautiful long hair

indicators.note: some of the word means only part of its letters, here a run from its middle

explanation.surface: A remark that many stage performers have lovely flowing locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of a woman's hair, often praised in poetry.

clue.text: The ruler seems worried about public relations

indicators.note: about means around, so the anagram goes round the abbreviation
worried suggests being agitated or disturbed, so the letters of seems are shuffled

explanation.surface: A head of state looks anxious about her press image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges the letters to EMESS, and 'about' wraps that round the abbreviation, splitting it EM...ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female sovereign or the wife of an emperor, someone who reigns.

clue.text: A quarter did away with 23

parts.note: south is one of the four quarters of the compass, abbreviated S
to do away with someone is to kill them

explanation.surface: A district of town murdered someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 23 Down, ADEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skilled means being expert or proficient, which is what adept means.

clue.text: Pole long past youth was in demand

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
someone long past their youth is elderly

explanation.surface: An elderly Polish person was popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality but gives S, one of the two poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that sold well found plenty of buyers, so they were wanted by the public.

clue.text: Gaining nothing by a musical performance

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: A show earns no money from a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music, a form of sung theatrical show.

clue.text: Underworld directions followed verbal exchanges!

indicators.note: followed means the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the name of the underworld itself
courses are directions taken, as a ship's course

explanation.surface: Instructions from gangsters were followed by heated talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' suggests gangsters but means DIS, the classical realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourses are spoken or written discussions, conversations on a subject.

clue.text: Close around a boy at certain times

indicators.note: around means the word for close surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to seal something is to close it
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone shuts a door around a lad at set hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal; 'Close' looks like an adjective meaning near but is the verb shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal things happen only during particular parts of the year.

clue.text: Relish talk which others find offensive

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys rude conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a condiment like ketchup, and cheeky, impertinent speech is also called this.

clue.text: Soft grain, inferior but still of much value

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
rice is a cereal grain
less means inferior or lower in rank

explanation.surface: Some cheap, inferior grain turns out to be worth a lot anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond any price is so valuable it cannot be bought.

clue.text: Intelligence shown

parts.note: intelligence here means news or information, and shown means screened, as at a cinema

explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short film of current events shown in cinemas, so it is information put on screen.

clue.text: The military man's high-hat!

parts.note: high-hat suggests a snob, but read literally it is a tall cap worn by soldiers

explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall cylindrical military cap with a peak and plume.

clue.text: Teenager creating a scene told off

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A youngster making a fuss gets a scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges A SCENE TOLD; 'creating' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person between childhood and adulthood, typically aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Scoops out river swans

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Swans on a river dig into the water with their beaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Female swans are called pens; the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Scooping out a hollow makes it go further down.

clue.text: Consequence of a cardinal's address

explanation.surface: The result of how a senior churchman is spoken to.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequence can mean importance or high standing, and Your Eminence is the form used when speaking to a cardinal.

clue.text: Presenter getting cross about brown reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the whole assembled piece is read backwards
about means the word for cross goes around the colour

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: An angry host thinks about a suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' builds ROTANOD, and 'reflection' turns that whole piece back to front; 'cross' looks like angry but is a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A donator is one who gives or bestows something, a donor.

clue.text: Drier ripping shirt, row ensues

indicators.note: ensues means follows, so the second piece comes after the anagram
ripping tears the word shirt apart so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Someone tears a shirt in a drier and a quarrel follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripping' turns SHIRT into THIRS; 'row' looks like a quarrel but means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thirstier means wanting a drink more, being more parched.

clue.text: Allowing for rental

explanation.surface: Permission to let a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting is permitting something, and a letting is also a property available to rent.

clue.text: Dispute profits always

parts.note: gains are profits
ay, or aye, is an old word for ever

explanation.surface: An argument about whether profits last for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict a claim.

clue.text: Dress material upset an idle egghead

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters of an idle are rearranged

parts.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: A lazy intellectual is annoyed about some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' suggests a scholar but supplies the first letter of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaine is a light woollen fabric, from French mousseline de laine, used for women's clothes.

clue.text: A Continental city medico needs change

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medico

indicators.note: change means the letters of needs are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor in a European town needs some coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges the letters into ESDEN; 'needs' looks like a verb in the surface but is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is a city in eastern Germany, on mainland Europe.

clue.text: Labour wants to retain about fifty

indicators.note: about here means the word for retain goes around the numeral

parts.note: to save something is to keep or retain it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: The Labour party hopes to hold on to about fifty seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party but is a verb meaning toil.
explanation.definitionFit: To slave is to work very hard, to toil.

clue.text: There's only a small section for 5

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, a section of an organisation

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being given only a tiny space.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 5 Down, SKILLED; 'small' signals the abbreviation of department.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is expert and proficient at something.

clue.text: A perfectionist giving some thought to a catalogue

parts.note: an idea is a single thought
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A fussy person thinks hard about a mail-order catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues lofty principles and standards, often unrealistically high ones.

clue.text: Constitutional support a sovereign gets

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
a sovereign is a pound coin, and L stands for pound (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A monarch receives backing for the constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests a monarch but is the old British gold pound coin, abbreviated L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constitutional accords with the established rules and law of a state.

clue.text: A little scoundrel seeming quite otherwise

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A minor villain appears to be something entirely different.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means differently or in another way, as in 'how else'.

clue.text: Worked out cut without hesitation

indicators.note: without in the old sense means outside, so the word for cut surrounds the hesitation

parts.note: excised means cut out
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Someone trained at the gym and lost weight without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but has its old sense of outside, the container signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercised means trained the body, as working out at a gym does.

clue.text: Interrogate cook

explanation.surface: A detective questions a chef.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone relentlessly is to grill them, and to grill food is to cook it under direct heat.

clue.text: Counts up the little ones

explanation.surface: Someone adds up the children.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is to add figures, and tots are small children.

clue.text: Badly anger constituents generally

indicators.note: constituents are component parts, so the letters of the two words are taken as parts to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Voters are, on the whole, furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' suggests voters but tells you to rearrange the letters of BADLY ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken as a whole and on the whole both mean in general, mostly.
